title: An add at the text of a key that carries a local tag replaces that key's value
notes: A pointer token matches a mapping key by the key's scalar text (docs/edit-semantics.md, Refusals), so `/yes` reaches the key `!local yes`, and an add at an existing key replaces its value (`edit/add-existing-key-replaces`). The string `yes` is written plain under the core schema. No second key is added. The exact bytes rest on a kit convention.

provenance.reference: Found in oneyaml-python: setting the string key `yes` by value (not by pointer) added a plain key beside the tagged one in the native backend and wrote onto the tagged key in the pure backend. A value lookup and a pointer differ here by design; a pointer reaches the tagged key in both backends, which this case pins.
